question: What is the term used for pollination by wind?
solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Anemophily.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anemophily, **often known as wind pollination, is a type of **pollination in which pollen **is dispersed by the wind. The majority of **gymnosperms and the grasses, sedges, and rushes** in the order Poales are anemophilous.
 
• **Wind pollinated flowers **are:-
 
 
• ​There are usually** no brilliant colours, distinctive scents, or nectar **in wind-pollinated flowers.
 
• The** majority lack petals**.
 
• **Stamens and stigmas** that are exposed to wind.
 
• There is a **lot of pollen.**
 
• Pollen is** fine, smooth, and airborne.**
 
• **Stigma with feathers** to capture pollen on the breeze.
 
 

 
• **Wind pollination is anemophily**. Pollen is carried by the wind.**​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Flowers are tiny and unnoticeable**. Non-essential components are either **eliminated or minimised.**
 
• The **blooms have no scent, colour, or nectar**. The male flowers are more numerous in unisexual blooms. The stamens of** bisexual blooms are typically many.**
 
• **Large, feathery stigmas on anemophilous **flowers make it simple to capture pollen grains in the air. In **grasses, maize, wheat, sugarcane, bamboo,** etc., anemophily is rather typical. ​
